items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He had a staff of three people, including myself and a fellow who taught percussion.

ctx.x: Had he --he had had a stroke by then?

I think so, or shortly afterwards. Anyway -- and the same with the Vibration School of Music. His health didn’t permit him to keep that going. That was a short- lived entity. He had a staff of three people, including myself and a fellow who taught percussion. I think I was over there -- I taught one session. Then it just fizzled out so it didn’t have any impact at all. Rahsaan may have taught a couple of sessions, but his health was the reason for the fact that he couldn’t continue. The Jazz and People’s Movement…

But I’m not even worried about where that branch of the media goes with it, because I’ve narrowed down my scope. I’m not concerned with mass media. I don’t think jazz is for everyone. I think one in ten people might appreciate jazz, and in that one person, I’ll zero in on. The other nine, I don’t know if there’s any prospects of their becoming jazz-oriented.
